name: Styrene-butadiene-styrene, SBS, block copolymer; average consumption mix; at plant
description: This cradle-to-gate, aggregated dataset is for 1 kg of SBS. It covers all relevant process steps and technologies for production of SBS used in liquid asphalt modification for paving and roofing applications, with high overall data quality. The unit-process inventory is based on primary data from four companies at six sites in Europe, Mexico, and the United States.
category: 31-33: Manufacturing/3252: Resin, Synthetic Rubber, and Artificial and Synthetic Fibers and Filaments Manufacturing

processDocumentation.timeDescription: Annual data were collected from participants for 2020. Results were published in 2022.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: Represents consumption of SBS in North America. It is produced in Europe, Mexico, and the US.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: The dataset covers production of raw materials, transport to the manufacturing facility, and manufacturing operations. Manufacturing encompasses anionic polymerization. In this process, monomers of styrene and butadiene are sequentially polymerized into polymer segments. An alkyl-lithium initiator reacts with styrene and monomers to form a “living polymer,” which can initiate further polymerization, Next, butadiene reacts with the initiator to also form a living polymer. These steps are repeated and block copolymers with multiple alternating blocks are formed. SBS may also be produced sequentially with styrene polymerized, then butadiene and then styrene again. These reactions take place in an inert hydrocarbon solvent in the absence of water, oxygen, or CO2. The average styrene content is 30% for this dataset, though values can range between 25% and 35%. Volatile matter, per ASTM D5668 is <1.0. Ash content is typically <1.0, per ASTM D 5667, though it can vary with method of supply (i.e., pellets, powder).
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: This process represents a RNA sales-weighted average of 6 facilities, owned by 4 companies. Participants and sites were selected based on willingness to participate. Products from the six cited production facilities comprise greater than 50% of SBS polymer for roofing and paving applications in North America.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: No inputs or outputs were knowingly excluded from the scope of analysis. Dataset mass balances.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Data were collected from 6 facilities and 4 companies. All companies were  Asphalt Institute (AI) affiliate  members at the time of the study. A small amount (1.61E-3) of 'Other Ancillary Materials' were not included in this inventory.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: The system boundary includes incoming transportation, direct emissions, material and energy use, as well as process waste management. The following are excluded from the system boundary: distribution to the customer, capital equipment, facilities and infrastructure, and support personnel requirements. Data were collected directly from 4 SBS manufacturers. Uncertainty was not calculated.
processDocumentation.useAdvice:
This process does not contain distribution to the customer because it will vary based on the location of the manufacturer and the location of the customer. User should include distribution of the product to the customer when using this dataset. 

Impacts from the inputs of styrene and butadiene are sensitive to the region of production. Ensure the region has been accurately represented by upstream datasets when modeling.

sources.name: WAP Sustainability (2022) LCA of Styrene Butadiene Styrene Block Copolymer

reviews.details: The review details can be found in the appendix of the above referenced report.

report.name: WAP Sustainability (2022) LCA of Styrene Butadiene Styrene Block Copolymer

processDocumentation.intendedApplication:
Situation A

The target audience of this model includes LCA practitioners, the asphalt pavement and roofing industry, and the general public. A full inventory of environmental flows are included; thus this unit process can be used for a full range of LCIA impact categories. The original study results were analyzed using IPCC AR6, TRACI, and CML LCIA factors.

This dataset is intended to be used for LCA practitioners to represent average SBS production. Without the appropriate ratio of region-specific styrene and butadiene inputs it does not represent the industry average consumption mix in North America.
